name: August 19, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 19, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Lingo called the meeting to order at 6:37 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Jake Lingo; Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb (arrived at 6:55
  p.m.), Alicia Peak, and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Chair Judy Villablanca

  ALSO PRESENT: Kate Manisco, Recreation Manager; and Chris Orosz, Interim
  Recreation Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Vice Chair Lingo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3—0; Chair
  Villablanca and Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recreation Manager Manisco reported the agenda for the meeting was posted on
  August l4, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  None.

  Vice Chair Lingo closed public comment.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion
  to approve the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried
  3-0; Chair Villablanca and Commissioner Goldfarb absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  PreviouslV Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 20, 2025 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting and the July 29, 2025 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Special meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthlv Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in July 2025.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 6:55 p.m.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Earth Friendly Management Policy
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly Management
  Policy activities from April 2025 through June 2025

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

  In response to Vice Chair Lingo, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated that
  essential oils have not been used or tested to control or mitigate the rodent
  infestation at Malibu Bluffs Park.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz clarified
  that park inspections were on natural turf grass not artificial turf.

  Commissioner Peak stated she was frustrated and concerned about the rodent
  infestations at the parks.

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated that staff were researching options to
  manage the gopher infestation at Malibu Bluffs Park following the EFMP.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated
that mitigation measures would help diminish infestation issues; however, it would
not stop them.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated the
Agents of Discovery application was available at Malibu Bluffs Park.

Malibu Equestrian Park Update
Recommended Action: Receive and flle a report on Malibu Equestrian Park
attendance and programs from May l to July 31, 2025.

Interim Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz
stated staff have contacted Trancas Riders and Ropers.

Public Speaker: Haylynn Conrad

Vice Chair Lingo closed the floor for public comment.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz
stated the City did not own equestrian equipment such as jumps. He stated those
items were previously owned by Trancas Riders and Ropers.

Commissioner Peak recommended staff collect attendance data from May through
June for the next two years.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated
the trail cameras could record the horse arenas to capture the number of equestrian
users.

Commissioner Skophammer stated the park should be improved to appeal to
equestrian users.

Commissioner Peak stated she supported programs by the Malibu Library and
suggested offering new programs that did not impact the property. She stated the
property could be renovated for new use and suggested waiting a year to determine
what could be done.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated that a year was too long and suggested to bring back
  an item related to programming in November.

  Commissioner Skophammer indicated agreement with Commissioner Goldfarb.

  Recreation Manager Manisco stated the Recommended Action was to receive and
  file the report related to park attendance and programs. She inquired if the
  Commission wanted to discuss program options for the Equestrian Park in January
  2026.

  The Commission indicated agreement to review program options, community
  outreach, and equestrian use research in January.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on Nature Walk and
  Storytime, Charmlee Wilderness Park hikes, and Summer Day Camps.

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Senior Center programs,
  Special Events, Aquatics programs, the Fall Recreation Guide, and Fall
  Registration with Rec Technologies.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak stated she wanted to discuss Skate Park memorial options and
  expressed her frustration over the timing related to the Temporary Skate Park
  closure and equipment surplus.

  Commissioner Goldfarb wanted public education on the bear sightings in Topanga,
  damaged trees, and invasive species on City properties.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated he wanted updates on major City proj ects every
  two months.

  In response to Recreation Manager Manisco, Commissioner Skophammer stated
  staff could provide project updates during the Staff Update section on the Agenda.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated
  the surplus of the Temporary Skate Park equipment was on the August 25, 2025
  City Council agenda.
